title: What If Your Gut Bacteria Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every bacterium in your gut vanished tonight? Your body is not built to be alone.
You carry about forty trillion bacteria, roughly as many as your own cells, and most of them live in your colon.
Your gut would lose helpers that make vitamin K and B vitamins. Without vitamin K, blood clots slowly.
Microbes also squeeze extra energy from fibre, up to ten percent of your daily calories. You would need more food to stay the same.
In germ-free mice, the immune system stays underdeveloped, with far fewer antibody-making cells, and ordinary infections become far more dangerous.
So the bacteria you try to wash away are quietly doing the work of a whole extra organ.
